Spiced Wine Hypocras

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 8-10Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Hypocras is a medieval spiced wine, a festive and warming drink enjoyed across Europe during celebrations. For the Feast of the Ass, a boisterous medieval holiday celebrating the donkey's role in biblical narratives, a goblet of this aromatic, sweet wine would have been a perfect accompaniment to the revelry and feasting, offering comfort against the winter chill.

Ingredients

  • 1 (750 ml) bottle dry red wine (e.g., Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey, or to taste
  • 2 cinnamon sticks, about 3 inches (7.5 cm) each
  • 1 teaspoon whole cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg (from 1/4 whole nutmeg)
  • 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) piece fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
  • Optional: 1/4 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • Optional: Orange slices or star anise for garnish

Method

  1. Pour the red wine into a non-reactive saucepan or pot.
  2. Add the honey, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, grated nutmeg, sliced ginger, and optional black peppercorns to the wine.
  3. Heat the mixture gently over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the honey is fully dissolved and the wine is warm but not boiling. Do not let it boil, as this will cook off the alcohol and diminish the delicate spice flavors.
  4. Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer very gently for 15-20 minutes, allowing the spices to infuse thoroughly.
  5. Remove the saucepan from the heat.
  6. Strain the hypocras through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth-lined funnel into a clean pitcher or heatproof serving vessel to remove all the spices.
  7. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired, adding more honey if needed.
  8. Serve warm in heatproof mugs or goblets.

Tips

  • For a stronger spice flavor, allow the spices to steep in the wine for several hours or overnight in the refrigerator after heating, then gently reheat before serving.
  • You can substitute brown sugar for honey if preferred, using 1/4 to 1/2 cup (50-100 g) depending on desired sweetness.
  • Garnish each serving with a thin orange slice or a star anise pod for an extra festive touch.
